cards.front: Recall a key point about Globalisation and the Financial Sector
cards.back: Globalisation is the increasing interconnection of world economies through trade, investment, technology, and multinational corporations.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Globalisation and the Financial Sector
cards.back: Benefits for the UK: cheaper imports, larger export markets, foreign investment creating jobs, spread of technology, greater consumer choice.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Globalisation and the Financial Sector
cards.back: Drawbacks: manufacturing jobs lost to lower-cost countries, trade deficit in goods, environmental damage, exploitation in developing countries, cultural homogenisation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Globalisation and the Financial Sector
cards.back: The four functions of money: medium of exchange (enables trade), store of value (holds purchasing power), unit of account (measures value), standard of deferred payment (enables borrowing/lending).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Globalisation and the Financial Sector
cards.back: The Bank of England sets interest rates, ensures financial stability, and acts as lender of last resort. Commercial banks take deposits, make loans, and facilitate payments.

cards.front: What should you know about economics exam tips?
cards.back: When evaluating globalisation, use the WIN framework: Who benefits?, Who loses?, Net effect (are gains worth the losses?). Globalisation creates net benefits but requires active policy to help the losers.
Cheaper imported goods, greater choice (e.g. Potential quality/safety issues with some imports)
Access to larger global markets (e.g. Face intense competition in those markets)

cards.front: What does UK manufacturing workers mean?
cards.back: Some jobs in export industries (e.g. Job losses from offshoring to cheaper countries)

cards.front: What does UK service-sector workers mean?
cards.back: High-value jobs in finance, law, tech (e.g. Less affected directly by manufacturing offshoring)
Higher tax revenue from successful sectors (e.g. Cost of supporting unemployed workers in declining areas)
Investment, jobs, technology transfer (e.g. Exploitation, low wages, environmental damage)

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Globalisation only benefits multinational corporations and wealthy countries. Correct: While MNCs capture significant benefits, globalisation also: lifts millions out of poverty in developing countries, provides UK consumers with cheaper goods, creates export-sector jobs, and enables technology transfer. However, benefits are unevenly distributed — London
Evaluate the role of the Bank of England and commercial banks in the UK economy.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: Globalisation and the Financial Sector
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Globalisation and the Financial Sector with precise business/economic terminology. Define key terms and state accurate factual information.
